descriptionChirho: A female parent, used both literally of biological mothers (Mary, Elizabeth, Herodias's daughter's mother) and figuratively of spiritual motherhood or personified cities ('Jerusalem which is the mother of us all', Gal 4:26). All three clusters represent identical semantics across languages: eng 'mother/mothers', spa 'madre/madres', hin माता/माताओं, arb أم/أمهات, kor 어머니/어머니들, swa 'mama'. The splits are purely morphological -- singular case forms (NFS, AFS, GFS, DFS), genitive constructions ('of mother'), and plural forms (AFP) -- with no semantic differentiation in any language.
